definitions.explanation: Describes something that causes fear or is frightening. Can also describe the feeling of being scared.

examples.japanese: その{映画|えいが}は{怖|こわ}かったです。
{暗|くら}いところが{怖|こわ}いです。
{怖|こわ}い{夢|ゆめ}を{見|み}ました。
{犬|いぬ}が{怖|こわ}くて、{近|ちか}づけません。
examples.english: I'm scared of dogs, so I can't go near them.

examples.japanese: {子供|こども}の{時|とき}は{夜|よる}{一人|ひとり}で{外|そと}に{出|で}るのが{怖|こわ}かったです。
examples.english: When I was a child, I was scared of going outside alone at night.

notes: Can describe both the thing that is scary and the feeling of being scared. Unlike English, Japanese uses the same word for both 'scary' and 'scared' - context makes it clear. {怖|こわ}がる is the verb form meaning 'to be afraid of'.
